summary:
The Bicol Region stands under the national framework of the Philippines. No regional statute, regional ordinance or regional enforcement body adds to or subtracts from that framework.

The one protection specific to the region is Albay province's sexual-orientation and gender-identity anti-discrimination ordinance, enacted province-wide in 2022. It covers Albay alone. No other province in Bicol is recorded as having an equivalent ordinance, so the protection a trans visitor can invoke against discrimination by private parties or local officials depends on which Bicol province they are in.

Gayon Albay LGBT Organization is recorded among the region's established local groups and is described as predominantly active in Bicol.
tangentialFactors:
The Albay ordinance is the only instrument at region level in the source material. Its implementing rules, complaint mechanism and enforcement record are not documented, so the practical weight of the protection cannot be assessed from the material available.

Travel between Bicol's provinces moves in and out of the only protection recorded at region level.
localsOnly: Residents of Albay have a provincial-level anti-discrimination route that residents of the region's other provinces do not. The recorded local organisation, Gayon Albay, is described as predominantly active in Bicol.
outOfScopeNotes: No source provides a finding specific to the Bicol Region beyond the 2022 Albay ordinance and the listing of Gayon Albay. The source material contains no data at region level on trans-specific violence, policing, detention, healthcare access or document processing, and the enforcement record of the Albay ordinance is not sourced.
